**8B.2 Research Note**
Kishida did translate his 2024 program into concrete policy machinery: priorities, budgets, councils, expert panels, legal reforms, and implementation mechanisms are all visible. The negative side is mostly about execution quality and political fragility, not absence of plans.

**Positive**
- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | Kishida turned his program into a concrete agenda with named priorities: disaster response, wage growth, child support, fiscal reform, digital administration, labor-market reform, and defense/security buildup. This is direct evidence of translating program into priorities and a timetable for the year. | QIDs: 8B.1, 8B.2
- [New Year’s Reflection by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/01nentou.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-01 | He explicitly linked policy execution to political stability and public trust, showing a governing plan tied to implementation capacity, not just rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.1, 8B.2
- [Prime Minister’s Office policy page: A New Form of Capitalism](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/newcapitalism.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 | The official policy page packages the ideology into operational components: wage growth, human-capital investment, labor reform, redistribution, and middle-class expansion. This is the clearest institutionalized program statement. | QIDs: 8B.1, 8B.2
- [The 2024 revised New Form of Capitalism and Basic Economic Policy package](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/21keizai.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-21 | Kishida moved the program into a formal economic policy package through councils and cabinet decisions, including broad subsidies and structural-growth policy. This is strong evidence of institutional translation, not just goals. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Budget guidelines for FY2025](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-29 | He approved budget guidelines built on medium- to long-term projections, private-demand-led growth, wage increases above inflation, and EBPM/“wise spending.” This directly shows program-to-budget translation. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Expert panel on active cyber defense](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-07 | Kishida convened a 17-expert panel to design legislation for active cyber defense. That is a concrete institutional mechanism for implementing the security side of his agenda. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Long-horizon energy and industrial strategy meeting](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/02gx_leaders.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-02 | He brought business leaders and technical experts together with cabinet members to design long-horizon industrial and energy strategy. This is a direct implementation channel, not a vague promise. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Foreign-worker program reform meeting](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202402/09gaikoku.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-02-09 | Kishida implemented expert-panel recommendations through ministers and bills, showing a formal pipeline from advice to legislation. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Nuclear Regulation Authority briefing on Shika restart screening](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/14kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-14 | Kishida relied on expert regulatory screening and post-Fukushima standards for any restart, showing formal enforcement and safety oversight rather than ad hoc discretion. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Noto disaster response package](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-25 | The government used cash aid, housing support, and service restoration for disaster victims, with specific attention to low-income households, schools, transit, SMEs, and agriculture. This is concrete budgeted delivery, not just an announced priority. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Reserve-fund recovery follow-up](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-01 | Kishida reported multiple reserve-fund tranches restoring infrastructure, lifelines, housing, and livelihoods. This shows implementation through repeated budgetary disbursement and recovery administration. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [AI provenance and trustworthy AI policy](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/02ai.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-05-02 | Kishida translated concern about disinformation into a concrete governance agenda: safe, secure, trustworthy AI and provenance verification. This is a specific enforcement-oriented policy step. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [JapanGov fact-checking / information-origin verification](https://www.japan.go.jp/kizuna/2024/01/growing_importance_of_fact-checking.html) | JapanGov / Government of Japan | 2024-01-26 | The government quoted Kishida saying information-origin verification technologies should be developed and diffused. This is a concrete implementation signal for the information-integrity part of the program. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [August 14, 2024 LDP transition statement](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-08-14 | Kishida said the LDP presidential race should be transparent and that he would step aside and support the winner chosen by vote. This shows a concrete timeline for succession and an internal rule-set for transfer of authority. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1

**Negative / Mixed**
- [Reuters: Kishida to step down amid scandals and living-cost anger](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Reuters framed the exit as driven by scandal and living costs, which suggests the program was politically constrained and not fully converted into durable governing leverage. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1
- [Reuters: ethics committee and budget pressure](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362) | Reuters | 2024-02-28 | Kishida had to appear before a parliamentary ethics committee and manage the funding scandal while protecting the budget process. That shows the implementation agenda was reactive and partly consumed by damage control. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9
- [Reuters: wage gains real, but weak yen and scandals blunted payoff](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Reuters said the wage program existed, but external shocks and scandals prevented it from fully landing. This is negative on realized implementation, even though the policy machinery was real. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [Reuters: government downgraded economic view after weak data](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japan-downgrades-view-of-economy-on-sluggish-consumer-spending-3309375) | Reuters | 2024-02-21 | The downgrade shows Kishida’s administration was responding to weak conditions rather than steadily delivering on the growth plan. It is evidence of fragility in execution, not absence of planning. | QIDs: 8B.2
- [AP: legacy of compromise and factional politics](https://apnews.com/article/05926b50f4f5a83a631f779d906cf06d) | Associated Press | 2024-09-30 | AP described Kishida as compromising with powerful conservative nationalists to stay in power. That suggests coalition bargaining diluted programmatic autonomy and likely shaped which priorities were feasible. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.1
- [“Illegal foreigners zero” platform page](https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/) | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 | The tougher migration-control agenda shows a concrete enforcement focus, but it is mixed because it looks more like exclusionary control than broad programmatic delivery. | QIDs: 8B.2, 7B.9

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence of program translation into budgets, councils, expert panels, laws, and oversight mechanisms.
- I did not find equally strong evidence of systematic appointment politics or a comprehensive, published implementation scorecard for every major priority in 2024.
- The main negative evidence is about political damage, coalition compromise, and incomplete macro results, not about a lack of concrete plans.
